extracted.intended_audience: policy makers within DoD and the Marine Corps; Regional Contracting Officers assigned to Marine Corps installations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for applying OMB Circular A-76 to competitive sourcing / outsourcing of installation support services in the Department of Defense, covering classification of functions, the A-76 cost-comparison process, PWS/QASP/MEO requirements, solicitation/evaluation, timeframes, risks and lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy principle — Government should not compete with private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the process of governing, the Government should not compete with its citizens... it has been and continues to be the general policy of the Government to rely on commercial sources to supply products and services the Government needs." (OMB A-76 guiding principle)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching normative standard guiding A-76 competitions: prefer commercial sources where functions are not inherently governmental. Use this principle when deciding whether to pursue competitive sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of inherently governmental functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions that are "so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by Governmental employees" and therefore are not open to competitive sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions rely on factors including level of governmental control, ministerial nature of the function, and distinguishing oversight from recurring operations. Refer to the OFPP list (Appendix C) of inherently governmental functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads of executive agencies must submit to OMB a list of activities which, in their opinion, are not inherently governmental functions (per the Federal Activities Inventory Reform Act of 1998).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAIR Act requires annual inventories of commercial activities; it does not mandate outsourcing but informs which activities are candidates for competition under A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where a cost comparison is NOT required
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB A-76 identifies nine situations in which cost comparisons are not required, including categories such as National Defense or Intelligence Security; Patient Care; Core Capability (generally related to technical capabilities); Research and Development; No satisfactory commercial source available; Functions with 10 or fewer FTE; Current performance by Government exceeds generally recognized industry performance and cost standards; and Temporary authorizations for piece performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before initiating a cost-comparison study, determine whether the activity falls into any exempt category. For functions with small FTE counts or where fair and reasonable pricing can be obtained and employees reassigned, a cost comparison may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 of cost comparison — Develop Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS defines what is being requested, the performance standards and measures and timeframes of performance; the QASP describes the inspection methods, required reports and resources to be expended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS must be performance-oriented (state outputs/measures/timeframes), not limit service operations, not arbitrarily increase risk, not reduce competition, not violate industry norms, and not omit statutory or regulatory requirements. QASP complements the PWS but need not be published in the solicitation; competing offerors develop their own Quality Assurance Plans based on the PWS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 of cost comparison — Perform management study to determine the Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a management study to define the Government's in-house MEO that can meet the PWS requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Management Plan documenting the MEO should identify structure, staffing, operating procedures, equipment, inspection plans, and document assumptions used in developing the MEO and in-house cost estimate. It must reflect the scope of the PWS and document assets, QA plan, and Transition Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 of cost comparison — Develop the in‑house Government cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a detailed in-house cost estimate reflective of the MEO and PWS scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost estimate must include documented assumptions, labor, overheads, assets, QA and transition costs; these figures will be entered on the Cost Comparison Form and compared against proposed contract/ISSA prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4 of cost comparison — Issue solicitation (RFP/IFB) or inter-service support agreement (ISSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue the solicitation per the FAR, Service regulations and any other statutory requirements; depending on the service nature, use an IFB or an RFP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose procurement form appropriate to the requirement (sealed bid vs negotiated). Treat proposals with standard confidentiality/security protections; ensure the solicitation is aligned with the PWS and does not preclude fair competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 of cost comparison — Compare in‑house bid against proposed contract or ISSA price
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the in-house estimate (MEO) against submitted commercial or ISSA offers on the Cost Comparison Form to determine tentative award decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sealed bids open all bids including the in-house estimate and enter prices on the cost comparison form. For negotiated procurements use best value determinations comparing the most advantageous private sector or ISSA proposal against the in‑house estimate. Evaluate responsiveness and responsibility as part of the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 6 of cost comparison — Administrative appeal / protest resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an administrative appeal process to ensure all costs on the Cost Comparison Form are fair, accurate and calculated in accordance with A-76 requirements, and resolve protests from unsuccessful offerors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protest resolution is the final and unavoidable step; ensure transparency and procedural fairness to withstand challenges. There are no guaranteed steps to mitigate protests beyond following the rules and providing proper appeal channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: PWS must be performance‑oriented, state outputs/measures/timeframes, and must not indicate how the supplier should accomplish the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write PWS so it does not limit operations, arbitrarily increase risk, reduce competition, violate industry norms, or omit statutory/regulatory requirements. Poorly written PWSs are a known cause of later contract modification and cost adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: QASP describes methods of inspections, required reports and resources; it complements the PWS and need not be published in the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP is used internally to monitor performance; competing bidders will prepare their own Quality Assurance Plans based on the PWS. Ensure QASP aligns with performance standards and monitoring resources are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan / MEO documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Management Plan must document the best structure, staffing, operating procedures, equipment, inspection plans, assumptions used in developing the MEO and in‑house cost estimate, assets, QA Plan, and Transition Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, auditable assumptions and documentation since the MEO underpins the in‑house estimate and will be scrutinized during appeals and comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and procurement compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations must be issued in accordance with the FAR, Service regulations and other applicable statutory requirements; choice of IFB vs RFP depends on the nature of services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure legal/regulatory compliance in solicitation drafting and issuance; treat security and confidentiality of proposals as with other procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — responsiveness, responsibility and best value
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare bids for responsiveness and responsibility; in negotiated/best value procurements, evaluate proposals to determine the most advantageous offer against the in‑house estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cost Comparison Form for numeric comparison but include evaluation of non‑price factors where permitted (best value). Document evaluation rationale to support decisions against protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes for A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent A-76 changes shortened timeframes: single activity studies must be completed within 18 months while multi‑service studies have 36 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan study schedules accordingly; recognize these timeframes are ambitious and require disciplined project management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected savings and caution in projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical A-76 competitions showed savings varying from 27% to 36% in some cases, but GAO questioned DoD/OMB savings projections due to unreliable data, wage increases and poorly written PWSs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use realistic data, account for wage escalation, and ensure high quality PWS/MEO to avoid over‑projecting savings. Track post‑award performance and modifications that may reduce initial projected savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and management in the A-76 process
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify significant risk factors in contracting of services (e.g., PWS deficiencies, contractor performance problems, contract modifications, price adjustments) and develop mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate risk management tools into the planning and contract (contract type selection, QA measures, transition plans). RAND and other studies note contractor deficiencies often surface after award, requiring contingency and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize definitions of commercial/base support activities
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no consensus across Services on definitions of base support/commercial activities; GAO reported wide variation (Army 122 functions, Navy 37, others lacked standard definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop standardized, service‑wide definitions and consolidated inventories (per FAIR Act) to reduce inconsistencies and improve selection of activities for competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider all competition sources and organizational reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive sourcing under A-76 includes not only private sector offers but also intergovernmental performance or reorganizing the in‑house organization (right‑sizing, other government organizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing competitions, include ISSAs and internal reorganization (MEO) as realistic competitors; document alternatives and rationale in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select contract type with attention to risk allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The contract type used in competitive sourcing can impact the nature and amount of risk the installation commander must accept (e.g., fixed price vs award fee implications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate contract types against performance risk, incentive alignment, and oversight capacity. Ensure chosen contract form supports the PWS, QASP and risk mitigation approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and auditability for appeals and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: All assumptions, costs, management plans, and the Cost Comparison Form entries must be documented to survive administrative appeals, GAO review, and audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain comprehensive records of PWS development, MEO assumptions, cost calculations, solicitation decisions, and evaluation rationale to support decisions and defend against protests.
